Asking a referral should be easy.Imagine saying just “Hi” or “Hello” to get a referral.It sounds simple, but thousands of candidates make this mistake every day. They send a greeting. And they wait.The result? They get ignored.People are busy. If you want a stranger to vouch for your career, you have to respect their time.You need to build trust in the very first message.Here is a simple checklist to turn a "Seen" into a "Referral":✅ Skip the small talk.Don’t wait for a reply to your "Hi." Send your full request immediately.✅ Be specific.Mention the exact Role and Job ID you are targeting. Make it easy for them to find it.✅ Prove your skills.Attach your Resume and a link to your LeetCode or GitHub. Show them you can do the job.✅ Highlight your wins.Mention a Hackathon rank or a "Best Performer" award. Give them a solid reason to trust you.✅ Keep going.The response ratio is often 1:20.Don't take silence personally. Just keep improving your outreach.To make it easier, I have shared an exact template I use to get a referral 👇Hit like if you found this useful ❤️

My dad once said:“You spent ₹300 on that shirt because it was ‘on sale.’”I defended it. He smiled.“But when it comes to learning about money, it suddenly feels expensive to start?”That stuck with me.We rarely hesitate with impulse spends.New phone case. Weekend drinks. Food delivery.But when it comes to long-term money decisions?“I’ll start when I have more.”Saw a dad point this out to his son today.The kid spent ₹100 extra just to save ₹25 on delivery.“You found money for dessert,” the dad said,“but learning about money feels like too big a commitment?”Sometimes the best money lessons don’t come from finance books.They come from the person quietly questioning our carts, our orders, and our excuses.What’s your version of a “dessert logic” expense?CoinDCXhashtag#DadApproved hashtag#moneylessons hashtag#priorities hashtag#learning

I actually thought this was a bug in the code.As an engineer, when I see "₹1", my brain goes to: Glitch.Because let’s be honest. It is Valentine’s Week. The week where logic usually exits the system and inflation enters. Roses are 3x the price. Chocolates cost a fortune. Even a simple card feels like a subscription fee.So when I opened Instamart and saw Valentine’s goodies for ₹1... I didn't click "Buy." I paused. I thought, "Surely, someone messed up the pricing logic."But it wasn't a bug. It was a feature.For new users, the math is actually romantic: Fresh Roses = ₹1. Chocolates = ₹1. No heartbreak. No surge pricing. Just a quiet little love letter to your wallet sitting in the app.Well played, Instamart. You actually made a "cheap date" look smart today.
